explanation: Append the current value, then recursively visit the left and right children.
timeComplexity: O(n+1): one recursive visit per node and one append per value.
spaceComplexity: O(h+1) auxiliary call stack for tree height h, plus O(n) returned values. Worst-case h=n.
attribution: JavaScript port of the independently authored EPI Practice C# algorithm; no upstream reference code copied.
correctness: An empty subtree contributes no values. Assuming each recursive call returns its subtree in the required order, placing the root before both calls produces exactly root, left subtree, right subtree. Each non-null node has one call, so it appears once; induction on subtree size proves the traversal.
walkthrough: For the tree with root 8, left child 4 (whose right child is 6), and right child 10, emit 8, enter the left subtree and emit 4 then 6, then enter the right subtree and emit 10. Result: [8,4,6,10].
edgeCases: An empty tree returns an empty list.
Repeated values are emitted once per node; do not deduplicate.
A skewed tree has height n, so recursive stack depth can be linear.
